arms.arche_decider: arche_engine with its review pairs decided by nigeria-facility-decider-v1 (decide_facilities.py); the engine's matches stand
arms.arche_engine: evaluate_facility_master.py as shipped (Splink backend plus arche's comparators and distinctive-signal gate); match = matched, review = held; best per GRID3 facility
arms.exact: folded name and folded LGA identical, unique on the HFR side; matched only
arms.splink: Splink 4.0.16, DuckDB, link_only; comparisons JaroWinklerAtThresholds(name, [0.95, 0.88, 0.7]), ExactMatch(lga), DistanceInKMAtThresholds(lat, lon, [0.1, 1, 5]); prediction blocking on lga or the first four name characters; lambda from block_on(name, lga) at recall 0.7; u by random sampling (1e6 pairs, seed 0); m by EM on block_on(lga) then block_on(name4); matched at p >= 0.9, held at p >= 0.5; best candidate per GRID3 facility. Configuration written from Splink's standard comparison library before any held-out state was scored; run once on Kaduna to check it executes, not tuned

metrics.held: GRID3 facilities whose best proposal is held for a person
metrics.matched_without_twin: auto-matches of facilities with no twin in the state (not scorable)
metrics.precision: auto-matches that are the facility's twin / auto-matches of facilities that have a twin in the state
metrics.recall_with_held: twins proposed at all (matched or held) / twins

no_pass_rule: a descriptive comparison, reported per state and pooled; no arm is declared a winner by rule
not_run: dedupe (needs active labelling by a person per run), Zingg (Spark, needs labelled training), commercial tools; named as not compared
question: On GRID3 v2 -> HFR health facilities, how do a naive exact rule, a standard Splink model, arche's engine, and arche's engine with nigeria-facility-decider-v1 compare in agreement with the registries' own id crosswalk?
states_why: the seven states held out of the decider's cross-encoder training; its combiner was fitted on about 1,700 labelled pairs from these states (roughly 1 in 5 of their twins), which favours the decider arm slightly
truth: GRID3 globalid = HFR global_id, both in the same state; no arm sees ids. Agreement with the registries' crosswalk, not accuracy: the crosswalk holds wrong links and HFR duplicates
